Just for Kicks: v​/Tetromino's Rotation System

Rotation System specs are important to skilled players of tetromino stacking games.
There are several popular rotation systems to select from, but none of them fit
the needs of a turn based game like v/Tetromino. Since players have plenty of
time to plan a series of moves, I aim to place more emphasis on "kicks".

A kick occurs when a shape is rotated near blocks or walls: If the shape's new
rotation collides with a wall or block the game attempts to move the shape a
space or two into a free space. Skilled players can exploit this behavior to
navigate shapes into tight spaces. Tetromino's rotation system needs to give
more opportunity for such maneuvers.

Tetromino's text mode places some restriction as to the types of rotations that
can be used. This is because one needs to know the center point of rotation
for a given shape just by looking at it. In a real-time game this isn't as
much of a problem because the player knows what the prior position was, and
can see the results of a rotation instantly.

I experimented with using a Unicode accent mark to indicate the spot around
which rotation of the active shape would occur. This allowed the rotation
center for some shapes be on the corner of blocks which increases the potential
kicks slightly. However, the visual result seemed too cluttered in text mode.

I've settled on using separate block styles to indicate blocks of the active
shape ◧, and its rotation center point ◩ in text mode. I'll need to add a
distinction to graphical mode as well. This means even the square shape
will have four rotations, and ability to kick, unlike in the more popular
rotation systems.
